title: THE SECURE PENDING BOX
goal: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
steps:
1. Imagine Container — Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible.
2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
3. Name Stored — Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support.
4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to the next task for today.
win: ✓ Someone else’s share moved back out of my hands.

• Use “Name Stored” on return.

title: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
steps:
1. Place Five — Picture a place using five sensory facts and one control feature: an exit, boundary, companion, or adjustable distance.
2. Rehearse Specific — practise entering through a specific cue and leaving on purpose.
3. Strengthen Safe-Enough — Strengthen the detail that produces the clearest bodily yes.
win: ✓ Progress no longer has to audition as perfection.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Strengthen Safe-Enough”; orient to now.
• If it flares, choose “Rehearse Specific”.
• “Rehearse Specific” moves memory toward then.
• Difference check: “Place Five” → “Strengthen Safe-Enough”.
• I can use “Rehearse Specific” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Place Five → Rehearse Specific → Strengthen Safe-Enough

title: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
goal: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
steps:
1. Apply Quiet — As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure.

title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
steps:

2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.

4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.
win: ✓ The practice has fewer leaks than it did a minute ago.
supports:

• Loop back? Use “Track Interval”.

• Difference check: “Choose Precise” → “Let Practice”.
• I can use “Return Instead” amid noise.

title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
steps:
1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.
win: ✓ I ended after five letters; do not score sleep.
supports:
• Exhale after “Jump Letter”; loosen the label.
• Skip replay; use “Flash Image”.
• “Flash Image” — the rule loosened.
• What lost power: “Pick Word” → “Jump Letter”?
• I can use “Call Object” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Pick Word → Call Object → Flash Image → Jump Letter
safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
steps:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.
win: ✓ The work can move without earning a flawless score first.
supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Clean”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Fix One”.
• “Fix One” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Continue Clean”: what changed from “Throwaway”?
• I can use “Make Wrong” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean
safety:
PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
goal: Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.
steps:
1. Ask Thought — Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move?
2. Check Protection — Does it protect something real?
3. Leave Me — Does it leave me more capable afterward?
4. Score Yes — Score each yes or no.
5. Thank Warning — If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.
win: ✓ Kept the warning, fired the sabotage, and chose a better adviser.
supports:
• Exhale after “Thank Warning”; slow the clock.
• Return once to “Leave Me”.
• “Score Yes” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Ask Thought” → “Thank Warning”?
• I can use “Check Protection” without rushing.

title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
goal: Some mental worlds persist through continuous subscription.
steps:

2. Time — For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let Existing — Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
4. Redirect — Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.
win: ✓ The construction crew clocked off; attention returned to the real room.

• Loop back? Use “Let Existing”.
• “Let Existing” proves the present returned.
• “Identify Image” to “Redirect”: what loosened?
• I can use “Time” to return here.

title: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
goal: Action can be sharp without inner warfare.
steps:
1. Define — Set the exact external behaviour required.
2. Execute — Execute it with full timing and skill.
3. Imagine Applause — Meanwhile, decline the running argument about authorship, resentment, or imagined applause.
4. Let Body — Allow the body act and the inner courtroom remain closed until the task ends.
win: ✓ The action stayed precise while the inner courtroom stayed closed.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Imagine Applause”, once.
• “Imagine Applause” keeps sensation as data.
• Difference check: “Define” → “Let Body”.
• I can use “Execute” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Define → Execute → Imagine Applause → Let Body

title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
goal: Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.
steps:
1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.
win: ✓ I let the message stay only in my mind.
supports:
• Exhale after “Wait”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Do Not Edit”.
• “Do Not Edit” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Wait”, compare “See The Person”.
• I can use “Say What Happened” without extra heat.
formula_flow: See The Person → Say What Happened → Do Not Edit → Wait

Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

WIN
✓ I let the message stay only in my mind.

• Exhale after “Wait”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Do Not Edit”.
• “Do Not Edit” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Wait”, compare “See The Person”.
• I can use “Say What Happened” without extra heat.

FORMULA FLOW
See The Person → Say What Happened → Do Not Edit → Wait

PAUSE
Stop and seek support if the exercise increases revenge thoughts, fear, or trauma.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
goal: A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.
steps:
1. Set A Time — Choose up to twenty minutes.
2. Tell The Story — In your mind, move through what occurred, what you felt, and what it means now.
3. Return to Now — End by naming your location, today’s date, and one caring action you can take.
4. Repeat if Useful — Try again on another day only if it helps.
win: ✓ The story got a container, an ending, and permission to stay private.
supports:

• Use “Return to Now” on return.
• “Return to Now” — the rule loosened.
• Before/after: “Set A Time” → “Repeat if Useful”.
• I can use “Tell The Story” without becoming the label.

title: CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE
goal: A prediction should lose influence when its decision window closes.
steps:
1. Picture Prediction — Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed.
2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, imagine a line through the prediction and picture the word EXPIRED.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.
win: ✓ The expired future lost its vote.
supports:
• Exhale after “Remove Vote”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Imagine Line”.
• “Imagine Line” — fear isn’t fate.
• Before/after: “Picture Prediction” → “Remove Vote”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Picture Prediction → Imagine Line → Remove Vote
safety:
PAUSE
Reopen only when genuinely new evidence creates a new forecast.

• Exhale after “Remove Vote”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Imagine Line”.
• “Imagine Line” — fear isn’t fate.
• Before/after: “Picture Prediction” → “Remove Vote”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” while fear stays loud.

FORMULA FLOW
Picture Prediction → Imagine Line → Remove Vote

PAUSE
Reopen only when genuinely new evidence creates a new forecast.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LIFE RETURNED TEST
goal: Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.
steps:
1. Picture — Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again.
2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.
win: ✓ Ordinary life regained enough value to deserve one move today.
supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose Behaviour”; no breath-holding.
• Catch restart with “Small”.
• “Small” — alarm isn’t command.
• At “Choose Behaviour”, compare “Picture”.
• I can use “Small” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Picture → Small → Choose Behaviour
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid loss imagery if it worsens grief, trauma, or suicidal thinking.

title: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
goal: Language can lower heat without lowering truth.
steps:
1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.
win: ✓ The facts stayed; the heat came down.
supports:
• Exhale after “Read Action”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Observe Behaviour”.
• “Observe Behaviour” proves motion is available.
• “Underline” versus “Read Action”: what eased?
• I can use “Observe Behaviour” before motivation.
formula_flow: Underline → Observe Behaviour → Read Action
safety:
PAUSE
Retain strong moral language when accurate naming is necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY

GOAL
Forecasts must compete for limited shelf space.

RITUAL
1. Picture Predictions — Picture the three predictions currently most relevant.
2. Enter Retiring — Any new prediction may enter only by retiring one, merging with one, or proving higher usefulness for a decision.
3. Cross Out — Remove retired entries from view.
4. Act Portfolio — Act from the remaining portfolio rather than unlimited mental possibilities.

WIN
✓ Alarm lost its 100-percent certainty.

• Exhale after “Act Portfolio”; drop the scoreboard.
• Restart detected: “Cross Out”.
• “Cross Out” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Compare “Picture Predictions” with “Act Portfolio”.
• I can use “Enter Retiring” without ranking my worth.

FORMULA FLOW
Picture Predictions → Enter Retiring → Cross Out → Act Portfolio

PAUSE
Expand the budget temporarily during genuine complex planning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
goal: Charge felt importance rent before it enters the decision.
steps:
1. Score Information — Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice.
2. Pay Felt — A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the priority list.
3. Allocate Attention — Allocate attention to decision impact instead.
win: ✓ Made vividness pay rent before it could buy my attention.
supports:
• Exhale after “Allocate Attention”; notice the room.
• Catch restart with “Pay Felt”.
• “Pay Felt” proves the present returned.
• Difference check: “Score Information” → “Allocate Attention”.
• I can use “Pay Felt” to return here.
formula_flow: Score Information → Pay Felt → Allocate Attention

title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
goal: Useful reflection needs a finish signal physiology can recognise.
steps:
1. Choose A Finish — Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.
2. Pair It — Pair it with one short answer in your mind and a time to think about it again.
3. Close It — Use the sensory finish only when the topic is truly closed.
win: ✓ The topic got a sensory full stop instead of another mental reopening.
supports:
• Exhale after “Close It”; notice the room.
• Skip replay; use “Pair It”.
• “Pair It” proves the present returned.
• “Choose A Finish” to “Close It”: what loosened?
• I can use “Pair It” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose A Finish → Pair It → Close It

title: RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE
goal: One problem should not carry the weight of the whole week.
steps:
1. Estimate Contribution — Name current stressors and estimate each contribution to body alarm.
2. Imagine Arrows — Imagine arrows from the present feeling back to its actual sources.
3. Stop Blaming — Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load.
win: ✓ The week stopped collapsing into one overloaded problem.
supports:
• Exhale after “Stop Blaming”; then keep moving.
• On return, repeat “Imagine Arrows”.
• “Imagine Arrows” proves motion is available.
• “Estimate Contribution” to “Stop Blaming”: what loosened?
• I can use “Imagine Arrows” before motivation.

title: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
goal: Emotion maintains itself through tempo as well as story.
steps:

title: GLOBAL LABELS NEED THREE RECEIPTS
goal: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.
steps:
1. Name Appears — When ‘I’m lazy,’ ‘I’m unlovable,’ or another global Name appears, demand three specific behaviours from the last month that support it and three that complicate it.
2. Replace Identity — If the evidence is mixed, replace identity with a narrower situational description.
win: ✓ The global label could not produce three clean receipts.
supports:
• Exhale after “Replace Identity”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Replace Identity”.
• “Name Appears” — the rule loosened.
• Difference check: “Name Appears” → “Replace Identity”.
• I can use “Replace Identity” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Name Appears → Replace Identity

goal: Personality may be a solution that outlived its original problem.
steps:

3. Design Alternative — Design one alternative strategy that offers the same protection with lower cost.
4. Test Low — Test it in a low-stakes situation before rewriting identity.

• Catch restart with “Design Alternative”.
• “Design Alternative” keeps worth off scoreboards.

title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
goal: When the doorway is the problem, let chance choose a safe entrance.
steps:
1. Number Doors — Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let Chance Choose — Use a random-number tool on your phone to choose one number. Do not pick again just because you dislike the number.
3. Enter There — Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Mark Progress — Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.
win: ✓ A random door beat the perfect doorway.
supports:
• Exhale after “Mark Progress”; release extra blame.
• Skip replay; use “Enter There”.
• “Enter There” keeps blame in proportion.
• Difference check: “Number Doors” → “Mark Progress”.
• I can use “Let Chance Choose” without owning everything.

title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
goal: Imbalance becomes negotiable after it becomes visible.
steps:
1. Plan Carries — Across a defined period, tally who initiates, accommodates, repairs, plans, and carries emotional follow-up.
2. Add Context — Include background for genuine capacity differences.
3. Use Categories — Discuss the pattern using categories, not accusations, and request one clear rebalance.
win: ✓ The invisible relationship labour became visible enough to negotiate.
supports:
• Exhale after “Use Categories”; keep both sides.
• Catch restart with “Add Context”.
• “Add Context” widens the evidence field.
• “Plan Carries” versus “Use Categories”: what eased?
• I can use “Add Context” before concluding.
formula_flow: Plan Carries → Add Context → Use Categories
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use the map to demand identical contributions under unequal circumstances.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

3. Finish Centre — Finish at centre and name the strongest contact point.

• Loop back? Use “Identify Instant”.

• Before/after: “Shift Weight” → “Finish Centre”.
• I can use “Identify Instant” before motivation.

title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
goal: Let an unmoving object prove that movement is not the whole field.
steps:
1. Rest Gaze — Rest your gaze on a stable line, corner, or heavy object.
2. Compare Visual — Compare its visual constancy with the motion inside your body and mind.
3. Don't Match — Do not make the inner movement match.
4. Let Facts — Let both facts coexist until the outer reference becomes usable.
win: ✓ Stillness entered the scene, so movement stopped being the whole field.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Facts”; notice the room.
• Shortcut: “Don't Match”, once.
• “Don't Match” proves the present returned.
• What changed: “Rest Gaze” → “Let Facts”?
• I can use “Compare Visual” to return here.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
goal: Urgency shrinks when hearing regains depth.
steps:
1. Identify Nearest — Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move Attention — Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let Far — Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.
win: ✓ Distance came back into hearing, and urgency got smaller.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Far”; slow the clock.
• Loop back? Use “Move Attention”.
• “Move Attention” puts facts above speed.
• Difference check: “Identify Nearest” → “Let Far”.
• I can use “Move Attention” without rushing.
formula_flow: Identify Nearest → Move Attention → Let Far
safety:
PAUSE
Use hearing protection rather than attention practice in unsafe noise.

title: CLOSE THE INPUT VALVE
goal: Consolidation cannot occur during endless intake.
steps:
1. Choose Defined — Choose a defined period with no nonessential news, feeds, podcasts, searches, or advice.
2. Keep Impulses — Keep a Notice for impulses to consume.
3. Observe Memories — Observe what memories, conclusions, or next actions emerge when fresh input stops.
win: ✓ Once input stopped, the mind finally had room to consolidate.
supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Memories”; mark the pause.
• On return, repeat “Keep Impulses”.
• “Keep Impulses” proves choice interrupted habit.
• Compare “Choose Defined” with “Observe Memories”.
• I can use “Keep Impulses” before autopilot.

title: WHEN DOES THIS INFORMATION EXPIRE?
goal: Data should not remain active after its conditions disappear.
steps:
1. Picture Expiry — For each influential input, picture an expiry condition: price changes, role ends, policy updates, health status shifts, deadline passes.
2. Expire Old Data — Notice any expired item. Stop letting it guide new behaviour until the information is refreshed.
win: ✓ Expired information lost its voting rights until it earns an update.
supports:

• Skip replay; use “Expire Old Data”.

• “Picture Expiry” to “Expire Old Data”: what loosened?
• I can use “Expire Old Data” before autopilot.

goal: Difficulty can signal growth, danger, novelty, or bad design.
steps:

• I can use “Stop Novelty” without obeying thought.

title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING
goal: Perceiver and perceived need not stay rigidly opposed.
steps:
1. Choose Simple — Choose a simple object or sound.
2. Attend Time — Attend at the shared time to its qualities and the act of perceiving.
3. Place Reality — Refuse to place all reality on either side.
4. Let Relationship — Let the relationship event—seeing or hearing—become primary for several seconds.
win: ✓ Seeing became a relationship, not a rigid split.
supports:
• Exhale after “Let Relationship”; watch the thought.
• If it flares, choose “Place Reality”.
• “Place Reality” proves thought is observable.
• Look back: “Choose Simple” → “Let Relationship”.
• I can use “Attend Time” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Choose Simple → Attend Time → Place Reality → Let Relationship

title: WHAT MATERIAL CONSEQUENCE DOES STATUS ACTUALLY HAVE?
goal: Rank signals can feel like survival events long after they stop being one.
steps:
1. Describe Status — Say the status loss without prestige language.
2. Name — Name actual effects on income, access, authority, relationship, and safety.
3. Separate Embarrassment — Separate those from embarrassment or comparison.
4. Respond Proportionately — Respond proportionately to the material column.
win: ✓ I separated the material consequence from the status sting.
supports:
• Exhale after “Respond Proportionately”; drop the scoreboard.
• On return, repeat “Separate Embarrassment”.
• “Separate Embarrassment” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• “Describe Status” to “Respond Proportionately”: what loosened?
• I can use “Name” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Describe Status → Name → Separate Embarrassment → Respond Proportionately
safety:
